title: code-graph --boundaries ignores imports from code outside every declared feature
rawReport:
## Summary
`@demlik/code-graph`'s `--boundaries` pass only inspects an import when its importer sits inside a declared feature. Code outside every declared feature can import a feature's internals, e.g. `src/access-gates/rules/x.ts`, and even re-implement its logic, with no violation. Under incremental adoption, where one feature is declared at a time, most of the codebase is "outside", so the wall has a hole exactly where it matters.

## What I was doing
Relaying a finding from the ‹product›-rooted session (monorepo-55), which hit it on the first real switch-on of `--boundaries` in ‹product› (#6194, one feature declared). ‹product› is proceeding without it, using a semantic rule that covers flag reads, but its config can't be tightened until this lands.

## What I observed
- The boundaries pass skips any import edge whose importer is in no declared feature.
- With only `access-gates` declared, a file outside it can import `src/access-gates/rules/x.ts` directly, and `--boundaries --ci` stays green.
- Features already guard each other: an importer inside feature A reaching into feature B's internals is flagged. Only the outside → feature direction is unchecked.

## Why it matters
Incremental adoption is the only realistic way to switch boundaries on in an existing repo, and it's exactly the case this gap defeats. A boundary that only binds code already inside another boundary guards almost nothing on day one.

## Pointers
- packages/code-graph/src/boundaries/ (the pass, its rules, the ceiling ratchet shared with `--collapse`, src/ratchet/scope-count.ts)
- PR #349 (#344), which introduced `--boundaries`
- ‹product› #6194 (the switch-on that found it)

## Suggested next step (non-binding)
Rule B4: an importer outside every declared feature, and outside the configured shared/`lib` area, may import a feature only through `<feature>/index.ts`. Count violations under the same per-scope ceiling ratchet, so existing debt can be frozen and ratcheted down. Add fixture tests covering: outside → index (allowed); outside → internal (violation); lib → internal (allowed, if lib is exempt); a ceiling that freezes the current count.

---

enriched:
## Pitch

**Problem:** `code-graph --boundaries` only judges an import whose importer sits inside a declared feature or a `lib` folder. Under incremental adoption (one feature declared, the rest of the tree undeclared) almost every importer is outside, so a file anywhere else can reach into `src/<feature>/<internal>.ts` and `--boundaries --ci` stays green. ‹product› hit this on its first switch-on and cannot tighten its config until it lands.
**Arc:** Code coordinates
**Appetite:** 1 cycles
**Rabbit-holes:** Widening B4 into a general "undeclared code" policy (per-folder exemptions, globs, allowlists); splitting the ratchet into per-rule ceilings; re-shaping `placeOf` for files outside `src/`.
**No-gos:** No change to B1/B2/B3 verdicts; no new config keys; no ‹product›-specific names in code, fixtures or docs.

## Scope (v1)

Add rule **B4** to the boundaries pass in `packages/code-graph/src/boundaries/`: an importer that is in no declared feature of its scope and is not in a configured `lib` folder may import a feature only through `src/<feature>/index.ts`. Anything else in the feature (including its `rules/`) is a B4 violation.

What main does today (read at `origin/main`):

- `analyze.ts` `analyzeBoundaries` classifies every module with `placeOf` into `feature` / `lib` / `elsewhere`, then `if (fromPlace.kind === "elsewhere") continue;` — the outside importer is never looked at. `violationOf`'s `case "elsewhere": return null;` is the second place the gap lives.
- The shared area is `BoundaryRulesSchema.lib` in `rules.ts` (top-level folders under `src/`, default `["lib"]`). `lib` importers are already judged by **B3** (`lib-imports-feature`), which flags a `lib` import of *any* feature file, index included. B4 must not fire for `lib` importers; B3 stays exactly as it is.
- Zones come from `zoneOf`: only `src/<feature>/index.ts` is `index`; everything else is `rules` or `internal`. B4 allows `index` only, mirroring B1.
- The ratchet (`gate.ts` + `src/ratchet/scope-count.ts`) counts **one number per scope**, `report.violations.length`, against `boundary-ceilings.json`. There is no per-rule ceiling. "Counted under the existing ratchet" means B4 violations join that per-scope count; the rule id lives in the violation's `kind` and in the render tag, not in the ceilings file.
- `render.ts` maps kind → rule id in `ruleOf` (`B1`–`B3`) and the target in `targetOf`; both are exhaustive `never` switches, so a new kind has to be added there.

Triage note: "outside every declared feature" is read here as every importer `placeOf` calls `elsewhere` in a declared scope, meaning any loaded file that is not under `src/<feature>/` or `src/<lib>/`, including loaded files outside `src/`. That matches the issue's wording and the existing `Place` union. If that turns out too broad for test directories, narrowing it is a follow-up, not this PR.

Triage note: the existing test `"leaves a file outside every feature and lib unjudged"` in `boundaries.test.ts` pins exactly the gap this closes (fixture `src/index.ts` imports `./findings/store/repo.js`). It gets inverted, not deleted. The fixture's recorded ceiling goes 4 → 5 as a result.

Triage note: adopters' `boundary-ceilings.json` counts rise on upgrade wherever outside→internal imports exist, so `--ci` reports EXCEEDED until they re-run `--write-ceilings`. The changeset says so.

Searched open issues for "code-graph boundaries outside feature import internal" and "code-graph --boundaries rules ratchet": nothing owns this surface (hits were #384 loader memory, #381 codegraph index, #387 structure-sweep), so this stays standalone.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `BoundaryViolation` in `packages/code-graph/src/boundaries/analyze.ts` gains a fourth kind for B4 (e.g. `outside-imports-feature-internal`) carrying `from`, `to`, `toFeature`, `specifier`, `typeOnly`, and `analyzeBoundaries` no longer skips `elsewhere` importers.
- [ ] An importer outside every declared feature and outside every `lib` folder that imports `src/<feature>/index.ts` produces no violation (fixture test).
- [ ] An importer outside every declared feature and outside every `lib` folder that imports any other file of a declared feature, including its `rules/`, produces exactly one B4 violation per edge (fixture test).
- [ ] A `lib` importer reaching a feature's internal file produces no B4 violation; it still produces its existing B3 `lib-imports-feature` violation and nothing else (fixture test).
- [ ] The existing B1, B2 and B3 fixture assertions pass with the same verdicts; the only change to the existing "reports each kind once" expectation is the added B4 row.
- [ ] B4 violations are counted in the per-scope `boundary-ceilings.json` ratchet: a test records the ceiling with `--write-ceilings` including the B4 violation, `--ci` then passes, and adding one more outside→internal edge fails `--ci` EXCEEDED.
- [ ] `render.ts` tags B4 violations `B4` in the human view (`ruleOf`, `targetOf` extended, exhaustiveness kept), with a test asserting the rendered line.
- [ ] `packages/code-graph/README.md` `--boundaries` row names **B4** alongside B1–B3, and states that `lib` importers are judged by B3, not B4.
- [ ] A `minor` changeset for `@demlik/code-graph` in `.changeset/` describes B4 and notes that existing boundary ceilings may need a `--write-ceilings` re-record.
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` pass.

### No-gos

- No change to B1, B2 or B3 verdicts on any input.
- No new keys in `BoundaryRulesSchema` or in the ceilings file format; B4 reuses `features` and `lib` as they are.
- No per-rule ceilings; B4 shares the existing per-scope count.
- No ‹product› names (paths, feature names, repo references) in code, fixtures, README or changeset.
